correctness.rationale: For X=K_p\{a}, Y=K_q\{b}, true-twin pairs have exactly their two endpoints as distinguishing vertices. Thus k>=3 impossible, k=2 forces X∪Y, k=1 permits at most one omitted in each. With p,q>=3 the remaining landmarks on both sides distinguish path/path, path/nonattachment and cross-side pairs. Direct factorization gives x^(p+q-4)(x+p-1)(x+q-1)(1+x)^(ell+1) and x^(p+q-2)(1+x)^(ell+1). Independently constructed shortest-path matrices, exhaustively checked 65,856 set/k decisions over 3<=p,q<=5 and 1<=ell<=3. Infinity proof rests on twin/distance argument, not finite checks.
